---
title: "Compiling models"
---

CmdStan turns each Stan program into a native executable. CmdStanPHP builds that executable when you create a model, records how it was built, and refuses to run it once it no longer matches the program.

## Create a model

```php
CmdStan\check_syntax_stan_file('model.stan', pedantic: true);
$model = CmdStan\cmdstan_model('model.stan', cppOptions: ['STAN_THREADS' => true], quiet: false);
```

`cmdstan_model()` compiles the model, or reuses an up-to-date executable, before it returns. There is no separate `compile()` step. The executable goes beside the Stan file, or into the directory given as `dir`. `quiet: false` reports whether the model is compiled and why. `check_syntax_stan_file()` runs only stanc, so it reports syntax errors without a C++ build.

`compile_stan_file('model.stan')` builds an executable without creating a model object and returns its path.

To run an executable without its Stan program, pass `exeFile` alone, as in `cmdstan_model(exeFile: 'bin/bernoulli')`. Nothing is built, and the build arguments are refused. `stanFile` and `exeFile` cannot be combined.

## Build options

`cppOptions` are make variables for this model's build, such as `['STAN_THREADS' => true]` for within-chain threading. `false` turns an option off even when CmdStan's `make/local` turns it on. `stancOptions` are stanc flags, such as `['O1']`. `includePaths` lists directories searched by `#include`, and `userHeader` names a C++ header with external function definitions. The [API reference](api.qmd#model-methods) lists the accepted values.

## When a model is rebuilt

Compiling writes a hidden build record beside the executable, such as `.bernoulli.cmdstanphp.json` beside `bernoulli`. The record holds hashes of the Stan program and its `#include` files, the user header, and CmdStan's `make/local`. It also holds the `cppOptions`, the `stancOptions`, and the CmdStan installation that built the executable. The next `cmdstan_model()` call rebuilds when one of these changed, and `quiet: false` names the change. A missing or unreadable record also causes a rebuild. `forceRecompile: true` rebuilds in any case.

Builds run on a temporary copy of the program, and the result is installed by renaming it into place. A failed build leaves the previous executable and its record in place.

Some changes cannot be detected: a new C++ compiler, a makefile included from `make/local`, or a header included from the user header. Compiling prints a note about the last two. Use `forceRecompile: true` after such a change. Switching shared CmdStan settings may also need `rebuild_cmdstan()`.

## Stale executables

Before each run, a model checks that its executable is still the one built from the current program. If the Stan file, an include, the user header, `make/local`, or CmdStan changed, the run throws `StaleExecutableException` with the reasons. Call `cmdstan_model()` again to rebuild. The Stan file must therefore exist whenever the model runs. `$model->isCurrent()` makes the same check without throwing, and `$model->buildInfo()` shows how the executable was built.

The check compares the file status (inode, size, and modification and change times) of every file the build depends on. When none changed, it skips hashing and the stanc call.

## Several processes

Processes that create the same model at the same time, such as queue workers after a deploy changes a `.stan` file, build it once. Building holds an exclusive lock on a second hidden file, `.<exe>.cmdstanphp.lock`, which is never removed. The other processes wait, then find the new executable current. Checking an executable holds the same lock shared, so a check never sees an executable and record that another process is midway through replacing.

`forceRecompile: true` still rebuilds in every process, one after another. Locking needs a file system with working `flock()`. A model in a read-only directory is checked without the lock.

## Version control

If your `.gitignore` ignores model executables, ignore the hidden files too:

```text
.*.cmdstanphp.json
.*.cmdstanphp.lock
```

The record uses CmdStanR's format under a different name, so CmdStanR's `.<exe>.cmdstanr.json` and this package's record never overwrite each other.
